annotations.description: Played Forest instead of Thriving Bluff on turn 1. Since there are no 1-mana plays in hand, turn 1 is the ideal time to play a tapped land. Playing Thriving Bluff now (choosing green) costs nothing this turn, whereas playing it later will waste mana on a turn where the player wants to curve out.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Bluff (choosing green) on turn 1 to get the tapped land out of the way, saving untapped lands for turns where mana matters.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain when nothing is castable this turn anyway. Thriving Bluff enters tapped, so it should be played now when the tempo loss doesn't matter. Thriving Bluff choosing green would provide a crucial second green source for Domesticated Hydra (2GG) while the three Mountains in hand cover red for Rapacious Dragon and Welding Sparks.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Bluff (choosing green) since it enters tapped and no spells are castable this turn regardless. This sequences tapped lands optimally and provides a second green source for Domesticated Hydra.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Nessian Hornbeetle into an empty board. The opponent has no creatures to block, so this is 2 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and didn't declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Nessian Hornbeetle for 2 unblockable damage.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Fertilid ({2}{G} = 3 mana) with only 2 untapped lands (Forest + Swamp), resulting in a rollback and no spell being cast. Wight of Precinct Six ({1}{B} = 2 mana) was castable and would have put another body on the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Fertilid, which was rolled back due to insufficient mana, resulting in no action.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wight of Precinct Six for {1}{B} using Forest and Swamp to develop the board.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Forest slightly reduces flexibility for casting Domesticated Hydra (2GG) on turn 4. With Forest played now, any of Mountain, second Mountain, or Thriving Bluff (choosing green) would work on turn 4 to enable the Hydra. With Mountain played now, only Forest specifically enables the turn 4 Hydra.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as the third land
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest to maximize flexibility for casting Domesticated Hydra on turn 4, since having 2 green sources by turn 4 is the key constraint

annotations.description: Timed out and passed without casting the only available spell. Nessian Hornbeetle grows with +1/+1 counters when the opponent controls a 4+ power creature, so it gets harder to remove over time. However, saving Welding Sparks for a bigger threat (especially after Rapacious Dragon would boost it to 5 damage) is a legitimate consideration.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting Welding Sparks on Nessian Hornbeetle
annotations.betterLine: Consider casting Welding Sparks on Nessian Hornbeetle to prevent it from growing, though saving it for a larger threat after deploying Rapacious Dragon (for 5 damage instead of 3) is also defensible

annotations.description: Using Welding Sparks (an instant) during precombat main phase on a 2/2 Nessian Hornbeetle rather than holding it. While the Hornbeetle can grow, it's currently just a 2/2 with no power-4 creature on the opponent's board to trigger it. Welding Sparks could answer a much bigger threat later, and as an instant, could at minimum be held until end of opponent's turn for maximum information.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Welding Sparks on Nessian Hornbeetle during own precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Hold Welding Sparks and pass the turn. At minimum, wait until end of opponent's turn to use it (preserving flexibility), or ideally save it for a larger threat. With Rapacious Dragon in hand coming soon (which creates Treasure tokens that boost Welding Sparks' damage), waiting has additional upside.

annotations.description: In a R/G deck, chose Blue for Thriving Bluff's color instead of Green. Blue mana has no use in their deck, while Green would provide valuable flexibility alongside their Forests for casting green spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Blue as Thriving Bluff's secondary color
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green, which matches their R/G deck and provides useful mana for future green spells

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Fell Specter (1/3 flying) when the opponent has no creatures on the battlefield. This is a free 1 damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Fell Specter for 1 damage to the opponent (16 → 15 life). There are no blockers on the opposing side.

annotations.description: Fertilid ({2}{G}) should have been castable with the available {G}{G}{B} from two untapped Forests and one untapped Swamp. The cast was attempted but rolled back due to mana payment failure, likely a mana selection error by the player. This resulted in no spell being cast in the postcombat main phase when a creature could have been deployed.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to cast Fertilid but failed to complete mana payment, resulting in no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Successfully cast Fertilid by paying {G}{G}{B} (one Forest for the green requirement, one Forest and one Swamp for the generic costs), deploying a 2/2 body with useful land-fetching ability.

annotations.description: Gem25P timed out and failed to declare any attackers when the opponent had zero creatures on the battlefield. Fell Specter (1/3 flying) and Wight of Precinct Six (4/4 with 3 creatures in opponent's graveyard) could both attack completely unblocked for 5 total damage, bringing the opponent from 15 to 10.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Fell Specter and Wight of Precinct Six for 5 unblocked damage.

annotations.description: Gem25P timed out and failed to declare attackers against a completely empty board. The opponent is at 11 life with no creatures, so attacking with Fell Specter (1), Ravenous Chupacabra (2), and Wight of Precinct Six (5) would deal 8 damage, dropping the opponent to 3 life — nearly lethal and setting up a kill next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Fell Specter, Ravenous Chupacabra, Wight of Precinct Six) for 8 unblocked damage, putting opponent to 3 life.

annotations.description: Timed out during precombat main phase with lethal on board (8 power of attackers vs opponent at 4 life with no blockers). Missed playing Forest and casting Pridemalkin before combat, which would have added a +1/+1 counter and more power to the attack. The timeout skipped available sorcery-speed actions including a free land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed priority without playing land or casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest, cast Pridemalkin (putting +1/+1 counter on a creature), then move to combat and attack with all creatures for lethal damage against the 4-life opponent with no blockers.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 4 life with no creatures on the battlefield. Gem25P has 8 total power across three creatures (Fell Specter 1/3, Wight of Precinct Six 5/5, Ravenous Chupacabra 2/2) — any subset dealing 4+ damage is lethal. Even the Wight alone deals 5 damage for the kill. The player timed out and attacked with nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers, missing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (or at minimum the Wight of Precinct Six) to deal lethal damage and win the game.
